title: Full Disk Access on Mac: Here’s what Apple must, and must not, do
snippet: We’ve seen a number of examples of why giving Meta’s Muse app full disk access to your Mac is a very bad idea, and yet another major privacy issue has recently been discovered. It’s now been found that Muse analyzes your communication with everyone in your life on an hourly basis. Apple is rightly concerned about the development, and in a blog post says that it will be introducing additional controls around the Full Disk Access feature that’s been enabling the problems … more…
fullText:
We’ve seen a number of examples of why giving Meta’s Muse app full disk access to your Mac is a very bad idea, and yet another major privacy issue has recently been discovered. It’s now been found that Muse analyzes your communication with everyone in your life on an hourly basis.

Apple is rightly concerned about the development, and in a blog post says that it will be introducing additional controls around the Full Disk Access feature that’s been enabling the problems … 

Meta recently launched its Muse Personal AI Agent for iPhone and Mac. Despite the obvious inadvisability of giving a Meta app unfettered access to everything on your Apple devices, the app quickly jumped to the top of the App Store.

Predictably, it wasn’t long before things started to go horribly wrong. Things haven’t gotten any better since then, with Wired reporting that security researcher Karan Joshi found Meta had instructed Muse to extract all of the information needed to construct a complete map of all of your relationships.

One of Muse’s instructions appears to be the ability for it to create “a page for every person in the user’s life.” This hourly process involves compiling data on family, partners, friends, colleagues, “collaborators,” and people you “follow,” the instructions say […]

“Where they live, what they do, the threads that recur (the apartment move, the shared savings goal),” the instructions say. They add, too, that the model could record the “dates that matter,” such as birthdays or anniversaries. A person’s history could include backstory like “the trip in March, the argument that got resolved, the milestone last week.”

Apple tightening use of Full Disk Access

You would think a permission prompt to give an app “full disk access” to your Mac would be self-explanatory, but it appears not. Even tech-savvy people have been granting this access-all-areas pass to their machines without appreciating just how dangerous a step it is.

Apple says the feature was intended for backup apps, but developers are now using it for many more things, including AI agents. The company has said it intends to “introduce additional controls” to ensure users fully understand what they are doing if they grant this permission.

Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.

Here’s what Apple must – and must not – do

Apple says it is “critical” to take this step, and I fully agree. When it’s become clear that the existing permission request doesn’t fully communicate the gravity of granting it, it’s essential that Apple ensure users genuinely understand what it is they are allowing.

What I’d like to see is far more explicit text advising people against doing it unless they are certain they understand the consequences. Something along the lines:

This app is requesting full disk access to your Mac, aka an access-all-areas pass to your data. Apple intended this feature to be used only by backup apps. If you grant permission, this app will be able to read all of your personal data, including all of your messages with other people. Giving permission is extremely dangerous and should never be done unless you are completely confident that you understand what the app will do with your data and that you have complete trust in the developer. Your default response to this permission request should be No.

Essentially, there is no wording that would be too strong. I’d also be fine with a one-off confirmation of the apps already given this permission.

	

However, what Apple absolutely must not do is to make the mistake it made with macOS Sequoia over screen recording. Sure, this is also incredibly dangerous and very strong warnings are appropriate, but what Apple did then was to force us all to confirm these permissions on a weekly basis, as well as after every restart. 

This was widely condemned as turning macOS into Microsoft Vista and imposing “a subscription you didn’t buy and can’t cancel.” In my view, Apple already goes too far in this direction with its occasional requests for repeated permission confirmations on iPhone. I gave Citymapper permission to access my location so that it can continue to provide directions in the background, for example, and no, Apple, I really don’t need you to check I still want this.

Yes, issue the strongest of warnings against granting full disk access, but if someone chooses to do so, then macOS must accept their decision. No forced confirmations, weekly or otherwise, thank you.

title: Utah Now Allows AI to Scan Your Face and Prescribe Acne Medication
snippet: The program is limited in scope and can only prescribe medication for acne.
fullText:
Robot medical help is fairly common in sci-fi, ranging from Baymax in Big Hero 6 to the surgical bots in Star Wars that put Anakin Skywalker into Darth Vader’s infamous black armor. Now, a subscription service in Utah has deployed the first AI doctor that can actually prescribe medication. 

Healthcare startup Nolla Health focuses primarily on skincare and acne treatment, and subscriptions cost $5 per month. According to Bloomberg, a patient uses an app to scan their face and fills out forms giving their medical history. AI software then analyzes the patient’s face and generates an acne severity score. If the scan and medical information indicate it, the patient receives a prescription for treatment from a list of eight approved treatments.

The pilot program is slated to last one year, Bloomberg reports. The first 100 prescriptions will be overseen by a board-certified physician before being sent to pharmacies. If that works, the next phase will allow the AI to fully treat 400 patients, with a physician reviewing the bot’s decisions weekly. The third phase involves the physician auditing at least 10% of written prescriptions once per month. 

			

More from CNET

A Nolla Health representative didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Michelle McOmber, CEO of the Utah Medical Association, told CNET in an email that Nolla Health didn’t need the Utah Medical Association’s approval to run this pilot program. 

“We never talked with them,” McOmber says. “The Office of AI Policy did have a short conversation with our current president, who is a dermatologist. OAIP also had the subcommittee of the Utah Medical Licensing Board look at [the plan] and comment.” 

The Office of AI Policy is part of the Utah Department of Commerce and is meant to guide responsible AI policies in the state.

McOmber says that this “very limited and very specific” use of AI is acceptable, but that the Utah Medical Association “would not be in favor of it being used for anything else at this time as it is.”

AI isn’t ready for more responsibility

Studies report that doctors, surgeons and mental health professionals are among the least likely professions to be replaced by AI. Even so, many medical professionals agree that the use of AI in the medical field is inevitable, either as a tool to assist human physicians or for simpler tasks, such as diagnosing acne or other skin conditions.

Some of those same medical professionals believe that AI in medicine is moving too quickly.

“We think people are trying to go too fast in using and relying on AI in healthcare,” McOmber said. “We do believe that AI, as a tool, can help physicians in different ways and that it will be used and even should be used.”

McOmber says human physicians should always be involved in patient care, whether it’s writing prescriptions or examining patients to diagnose conditions. AI in its current form is best for such simple tasks as gathering useful medical information and histories from patients, she says.

“Care decisions ultimately should rest with the physician in consultation with the patient,” McOmber says. “AI, if used inappropriately, can be very dangerous in healthcare.”

title: Google AI Edge Foresight for Mac turns scribbles into full notes using offline recordings
snippet: Google today announced its new EmbeddingGemma 2 model that can be used to “organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware.” To show off its potential, Google created an AI Edge Foresight Mac app for “intelligent notetaking.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced its new EmbeddingGemma 2 model that can be used to “organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware.” To show off its potential, Google created an AI Edge Foresight Mac app for “intelligent notetaking.”

EmbeddingGemma 2 “can help find a specific video clip from a voice memo, or search through hours of audio recordings based on a text query, all processed by a single, natively multimodal model.”

The 740 million parameter model is built on the Gemma 4 architecture and available with an Apache 2.0 license. This is meant to run locally “within tight resource constraints”:

With quantization, on a Google Pixel 11 Pro, EmbeddingGemma 2 requires as little as ~191MB active RAM for text-only weights and ~567MB for the full multimodal model.

To showcase, there are demos in Google AI Edge Gallery on Android and iOS. The bigger showcase is a new Mac app called Google AI Edge Foresight.

	

During video or in-person meetings, this notetaking app listens in the background so that you can just “scribble shorthand bullets for things you want to remember.”

The app, leveraging EmbeddingGemma 2, “enriches [that shorthand] into polished notes using the meeting transcript instantly.” The transcript and audio are processed entirely on your device rather than the cloud.

Another capability lets you “point Google AI Edge Foresight to your project folders, reference materials, diagrams, and calendar.” Supporting local files and Google Drive, this in turn lets you ask the app questions and quickly get back information.

It automatically understands your work without needing to manually organize your files, to ensure critical information is ready whenever you need it.

The chat feature offers “conversational retrieval and summary with your personal knowledge.” There’s also a Live Assistance capability that will “listen and automatically answer questions.”

You can download Google AI Edge Foresight here. This joins Google’s two other Mac apps in the family: AI Edge Gallery and AI Edge Eloquent (offline transcription).

title: Pixel 10a gets a $100 price hike, now starting at $599
snippet: Google has quietly raised the price of its mid-range Pixel 10a by $100, giving the device a starting price of $599. more…
fullText:
Google has quietly raised the price of its mid-range Pixel 10a by $100, giving the device a starting price of $599.

Effective as of today at the Google Store, Pixel 10a has jumped from $499 to $599. The reason is obvious, of course, with the current skyrocketing costs of components such as memory. Google has not officially commented on the price hike yet, though.

This follows Google issuing a price increase to each of its new Pixel 11 devices compared to the prior generation. 

When Google confirmed the Pixel 11 would be more expensive, the company said that this would eventually impact “in-market Pixel phones” which, at the time, we speculated could include Pixel 10a.

	

The 128GB base Pixel 10a is $599 as of today, with the 256GB model at $699. The updated prices have already kicked in at Amazon and Best Buy, and Google Store now shows Pixel 10a at $849 in Canada, £599 in the UK, and €649 in Europe.

	

In our review of Pixel 10a, we called the device a “well-rounded experience” for its $499 price, but a $100 jump certainly makes that a tougher conversation, especially considering Google’s mid-ranger is at this point using a two-generation-old chipset in its Tensor G4. But, of course, Google is far from alone here. Just this week, Samsung also issued price hikes across the Galaxy lineup including flagship and mid-range devices alike.

fullText:
Google Pixel was designed to be a premium smartphone effort, but that all changed in 2019 with the debut of the Pixel 3a. The budget-conscious launch went on to be a turning point for the Pixel’s history and, looking back, it might just be the single most important Google smartphone ever.

Looking back over the past decade of Pixel smartphones, I’m not sure you can point at any one device and say it was more important than the Pixel 3a. The original Pixel set the foundation, of course, and Pixel 6 launched Google’s efforts into a new era, but Pixel 3a gave Google a taste of what it was always after – market success.

The Pixel 3a almost immediately shot up to the top of best-seller lists, massively propelled Google’s US smartphone sales, and was the driving force behind setting Google’s first big shipment records. That success ultimately led to several Pixel A-series successors that have similarly resonated in the market. These more affordable devices just nail the fundamentals at a price that’s hard to beat, especially considering the cost of a Pixel 10a is only $100 more (annnnnnd now it’s $200) than the Pixel 3a originally started at.

Google is finding at least some success in the flagship market nowadays. Pixel phones are very much hitting their stride in 2026 not only in terms of design and functionality, but also in the market as a whole. I’d very much argue, though, that the Pixel 3a was the lifejacket that kept this project going. The failure of the Pixel 4 left scars on Google’s smartphone efforts, but the Pixel 3a’s resounding success was surely a huge deciding factor on what would come next.

	
	

And, in 2026, I think this phone holds up remarkably well from a hardware perspective. There are modern budget phones that cost just as much as the Pixel 3a did when it came out that feel a lot worse than this one. The Pixel 3a is long dead at this point with software support having ended in 2022, but its legacy lives on.

title: If Apple’s AI suggestions in Messages annoys you, there’s a solution coming
snippet: The current beta of iOS 27.2 includes a Siri AI “suggested actions” feature in the Messages app that some will consider useful and others find annoying. A developer who has found a number of unannounced features has discovered that Apple is seeking to keep everyone happy with a new set of options … more…
fullText:
The current beta of iOS 27.2 includes a Siri AI “suggested actions” feature in the Messages app that some will consider useful and others find annoying. 

A developer who has found a number of unannounced features has discovered that Apple is seeking to keep everyone happy with a new set of options …

Suggested Actions in Messages

Suggested Actions were present in the initial iOS 27 beta, but Apple later pulled the feature after complaints that some of the suggestions were rather random. It subsequently returned in the beta of iOS 27.2. Here’s how Apple describes it:

Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.

In the first example shown above, a group message chat contains a request for some shopping and to bring something left behind. The Messages app offers one-tap options to Add to Reminders and Add to Notes. In the second example, someone asks for specific photos to be shared, and the Messages app offers a button which leads directly to a search for matching photos.

Two ways to hide unwanted suggestions

Leaker pdfu found new controls in iOS 27.2 beta 3 to selectively toggle off unwanted suggestions.

These allow suggestions to be toggled off by category, or you can let Siri AI monitor which ones you do and don’t use, and have it automatically hide the categories you haven’t used in the last 30 days.

These options aren’t yet live in the beta, but we can likely expect to see them soon.

9to5Mac’s Take

I’m certainly one of those who found many of them more annoying than useful, while I know others who are big fans, so this change ought to keep everyone happy.

title: OpenAI details new text watermarking system for ChatGPT, Codex, and the API
snippet: OpenAI today announced how it will comply with the EU AI Act, which requires providers of generative AI systems to mark AI-generated text in a way that makes it identifiable. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
OpenAI today announced how it will comply with the EU AI Act, which requires providers of generative AI systems to mark AI-generated text in a way that makes it identifiable. Here are the details.

A bit of context

A few months ago, Anthropic sparked controversy when it announced that, to comply with the EU AI Act, Claude would start watermarking text by slightly adjusting its word choice.

In a nutshell, every so often, Claude chooses between words that would work equally well based on a hidden pattern, which Anthropic says has no practical impact on the meaning, quality, or readability of its responses.

Anthropic also developed a detector that can look for that pattern in a piece of text, and can tell whether it likely came from Claude.

The detector can’t be used to determine whether text came from OpenAI or any other competitor, since Claude’s watermark is generated using a secret key specific to Anthropic’s system.

At the height of the controversy, Anthropic stressed that Claude would not be alone, noting that several other major AI providers were also implementing marking systems to comply with the EU’s requirements.

Today, OpenAI announced its own solution, which relies on a similar approach, albeit with a much more limited rollout and scope.

OpenAI’s text watermarking system

According to OpenAI, “API customers globally will be able to opt in to text watermarking for select models” starting today, while the company “will add an invisible watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the European Union” in the coming weeks.

This means that in the API, text watermarking will remain off by default for now, while in ChatGPT and Codex, it will initially be limited to eligible users only in the European Union.

OpenAI also opened applications for access to its text watermark detector, which will initially be limited to approved researchers and expert organizations as the company works to evaluate and improve the technology.

And speaking of accuracy, OpenAI is very clear that the detection technology still has significant limitations, as it can produce both false negatives and false positives, particularly with shorter texts or content in specific domains, “such as mathematics, where there is less flexibility in word choice.”

Here’s OpenAI on textGrain, which is its text watermarking technology:

Our text watermarking technology, textGrain, adds an invisible statistical signal to the model’s word choices. Our detector looks for that signal to assess whether a passage contains an OpenAI watermark. More details about how textGrain works can be found in our technical report⁠, which will be updated with additional details in the coming weeks. We also plan to make the technology available in open source so that others can build on it.

The company also noted that, in addition to being harder to detect in shorter passages, the watermark can be significantly weakened by editing:

In an evaluation of 400-token passages, replacing 10% of words with synonyms reduced detection from about 92% to 66%. Replacing 25% of words reduced it to 17%.

Interestingly, OpenAI’s comparison of watermarked and unwatermarked text showed that watermarked outputs actually scored slightly higher on several benchmarks, despite the company saying it found no meaningful difference in overall performance.

OpenAI also stressed that, in addition to the false positive and false negative shortcomings, a watermark “does not measure human contribution,” “does not establish ownership or responsibility,” “does not identify the user,” and “does not verify accuracy.”

OpenAI added that “the absence of a detected watermark does not prove human authorship” either.

Finally, the company said it expects to revisit its approach as the technology, standards, and evidence evolve, while continuing to study how well watermarks survive editing and translation and whether they can more meaningfully distinguish AI assistance from AI authorship.

title: While VCs crowd into San Francisco, Endeavor Catalyst raises $320M for founders ‘elsewhere’
snippet: Endeavor Catalyst just raised $320 million to keep backing founders outside Silicon Valley. Half the profits go back to the nonprofit that finds them.
fullText:
Endeavor Catalyst has closed its fifth fund with $320 million in capital commitments, bringing the firm’s total assets under management to more than $850 million. The raise is good news for founders outside the Bay Area who risk getting overlooked as more funds focus squarely on AI companies in Silicon Valley.  

Endeavor Catalyst is the venture arm of Endeavor, a New York-based global nonprofit that has spent 30 years supporting founders outside major tech hubs. (It calls all those other places “elsewhere” throughout its marketing materials.)

The fund is run by managing partner Allen Taylor, a 20-year veteran of the organization, and managing director Jackie Carmel, who joined Endeavor Catalyst 12 years ago, along with a 16-person team. The official general partner, though, is Endeavor itself. What that means, says Linda Rottenberg, who co-founded Endeavor and helped start Endeavor Catalyst in 2012, is that “half of the fund’s profits go back to Endeavor, so every investment helps the next generation of founders who are building elsewhere.”

The bar for those founders is pretty high. A person first has to get into Endeavor’s network, where he or she can access Endeavor’s mentoring and extensive network, and that’s hard. Last year, the group says it screened more than 10,000 candidates and picked 88. The network now has more than 3,100 entrepreneurs in over 50 countries.

When one of those founders’ companies raises at least $5 million in a round led by another institutional investor, Endeavor Catalyst can join in on the same terms as that lead. The team tells TechCrunch that checks usually run $1 million to $3 million but can’t exceed 10% of the round.

Over the next few years, they plan to make 40 to 50 investments annually, investing in up to 150 companies altogether with this new fund, they say.

Taylor, via an email exchange, wouldn’t share numbers on cash-on-cash returns tied to its earlier funds, but he did point to some impressive-sounding numbers. Across all five funds, he says, Endeavor Catalyst has backed 437 companies in 44 markets. Eighty-three of those startups are currently valued at $1 billion or more, he says, and the unit has seen 39 exits and 11 IPOs.

Some of the venture arm’s most valuable holdings right now include four-year-old ElevenLabs, the maker of AI voice tools that was recently valued at $22 billion in a secondary sale (it was founded in Poland originally), and Bending Spoons, the 13-year-old Italy-based conglomerate that went public in July and that currently boasts a $26 billion market cap.

Other holdings include New York-based Reflection AI (founded by two former Google DeepMind researchers — one of whom was born in Greece), which is now valued at $25 billion; Checkout.com, whose founder is Swiss and which was valued last year at $12 billion; the African payments infrastructure company Flutterwave, valued this summer at $3.2 billion; and AI coding startup Replit, co-founded by Amjad Masad, who is Palestinian-Jordanian. Replit snagged a $9 billion valuation earlier this year.

Endeavor, the nonprofit, has especially well-connected people associated with it, including board members Reid Hoffman; Nick Beim, a career VC who has spent the last 25 years at Matrix Partners, then Venrock; and Edgar Bronfman Jr., the former head of Warner Music and Seagram, who chairs Endeavor’s board.

Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is a longtime friend of Endeavor, too, having gone to Harvard with Rottenberg. (Late last month in San Francisco, I sat down with him during a rare visit to the Bay Area that was organized by Endeavor and where he met with tech founders and Greek expatriates.)

Altogether, Endeavor Catalyst’s newest fund includes 400 limited partners, including Hoffman; famed hedge fund manager Bill Ackman; and the Dutch investment group Prosus. According to Taylor, roughly 30% of those backers are Endeavor founders themselves, including founders of Nubank, Revolut, and Checkout.com.

While so much attention is paid to what’s happening in San Francisco and its immediate environs right now, the bets of Endeavor Catalyst suggest what other investors may be missing, and Endeavor, with local teams and mentors in dozens of countries, seems particularly well-positioned to see it.

Indeed, about 90% of the venture arm’s investments are outside the U.S., it says. Europe is its fastest-growing region, with 12 new investments in the first half of 2026 compared with 14 in all of last year, though Latin America is still the largest. 

Repeat founders are also becoming a bigger part of the mix. Taylor tells TechCrunch that roughly 14% of Endeavor Catalyst’s fourth fund went to second companies started by Endeavor founders at the seed or Series A stage. With this new fund, the team expects that number will reach 20%.

Pictured above: Endeavor co-founder Linda Rottenberg onstage in Turin, Italy, earlier this month.

title: Nvidia Shield TV Pro is now $299 – a $100 price hike seven years after the Android TV box launched
snippet: The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched. more…
fullText:
The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched.

Nvidia Shield TV Pro made its debut in October 2019 and, to this day, remains one of the most capable Android TV streamers on the market. While certain aspects haven’t aged perfectly, such as a lack of AV1 support and others, it remains unmatched in other places.

That’s a big part of the reason that, even so many years after it launched, Nvidia continues to produce the Shield TV.

But the $199 price point is gone. Effective today, Nvidia Shield TV Pro now costs $299.99. Nvidia attributed the price hike to the fact that “the cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry.” Alongside the change in price, Nvidia has also ended production of the base Shield TV that was also introduced in 2019. The “tube” Shield has been out of stock for months at this point, but Shield TV Pro was just restocked at Best Buy.

	

Shield TV Pro at Best Buy

Early this year, Nvidia said that it would continue software support for the Shield TV for the forseeable future. 

Shield isn’t the only streamer going up in price as a result of RAMageddon. Google TV Streamer saw a price hike to $149 recently, while other devices including Apple TV 4K and various Roku streamers also saw price hikes earlier this year. 

AI is just great, right?

title: Spotify is getting more serious about selling enterprise software
snippet: The company launched technology.spotify.com, a new site that will make its internal tech available to outsiders.
fullText:
Spotify is formalizing efforts around its enterprise and developer tools business with Thursday’s launch of technology.spotify.com, a new site that will make its internal tech available to outsiders.

The company’s foray into this space is not exactly new. As Spotify points out in its announcement of the new site, it’s been offering different products to the wider tech community since 2020 when it open sourced Backstage, a platform and framework for building customizable developer portals.

It has also been selling its enterprise-focused software experimentation platform Confidence since 2023 and its enterprise software development platform Portal since 2024. Earlier this year, it began selling its developer tool for managing AI coding agents, Xirp.

While many technology companies build their own internal systems to help their developers work more efficiently, it’s somewhat unusual to see a company like Spotify sell those tools to other businesses. 

Spotify’s SVP of Technology & Platform, Tyson Singer, acknowledged that the company’s move into this space has raised questions.

“I get asked a version of this question every day: why is Spotify in the business of selling software?,” he wrote in a post on Spotify’s engineering site. “The truth is, the Spotify you know and love is more than a great streaming service. Behind our consumer app are hundreds of cross-functional squads shipping products and code day in, day out,” he explained. 

The new technology website will house the solutions Spotify has built to serve its own audience of 777 million monthly active users, including both open source and paid services. 

Though AI has made building such software faster, Spotify points out that this doesn’t necessarily mean it’s simpler — “the complexity, the cost and the operational surface area all grow with it,” Singer wrote. The company’s bet is that, despite AI’s advances, software development teams will still require certain core services, like those Spotify sells, which it says will be agent-ready.

So far, it’s unclear how much revenue Spotify’s enterprise sales are generating, as the company hasn’t disclosed those figures in its financial reporting. That could potentially change as Spotify makes a more concerted push into the enterprise market, turning what was once a side business into a more formal operation.

The technology website doesn’t include pricing; instead, companies can fill out a form to contact sales and discuss their needs.

title: Goodbye, Fire Tablet: Amazon’s New Alexa Tablet Is a Flashy Portable Entertainment Hub
snippet: The new tablets tie together the Amazon media ecosystem so you can pick up where you left off from just about anywhere.
fullText:
A new lineup of Amazon tablets has been announced, and the devices are designed for both work and play. Amazon Alexa Tablets combine cloud-based device syncing functionality, onboard AI capabilities and the entirety of Amazon’s media catalog, making them something akin to on-the-go entertainment hubs.

Each of the three Alexa Tablet models has an aluminum chassis, which will protect what’ll be some of the thinnest devices Amazon has ever released. More importantly, Fire OS and the Amazon Appstore are going away. Instead of a custom, forked operating system, the Alexa Tablets will run Android 16 at launch, and will upgrade to Android 17 in early 2027. That means these devices will offer full Play Store functionality, giving you access to plenty of apps that haven’t previously been compatible with Amazon tablets.

But the software capabilities are what I suspect will be the real draw. If you use an Amazon account on your computer, phone, TV or other device, it will automatically sync up with the Alexa Tablets. A dynamic tab on the home screen allows you to quickly pick up movies, shows, books and games wherever you left off. There’s also an algorithmic “For You” layout that shows you other content you might enjoy based off of what you’re currently enjoying, like a streaming model that pulls together every form of media in one place.

			

More from CNET

Avid readers will be able to access their Audible and Kindle libraries in one place, and a new Kindle mode also silences notifications, turns down blue light and enhances battery life. I got a firsthand look at the e-ink and color paper modes at an in-person event in New York and was impressed with how the pages looked on-screen. The texture of the display is sufficiently papery, too. (TCL’s Nxtpaper devices may soon be given a run for their money.)

The Alexa Plus AI assistant may not be the speediest helper, but it has all of your Amazon account’s personal information at its virtual fingertips.Tyler Graham/CNET

Each Alexa Tablet is deeply integrated with Alexa Plus AI, allowing you to converse with it and pull answers from Amazon’s Silk browser on the fly. Opting into on-screen intelligence allows the generative model to see what’s on the display. It can answer questions about images in a browser, locate listings for specific products shown in a social media video and more. During the product demonstration, Alexa Plus took upwards of half a minute to respond to complicated prompts, but the onboard model responded accurately to verbal requests about managing a personal calendar and finding nearby restaurants based on dietary restrictions.

Kevin Keith, vice president of Amazon’s devices team, told me that the new lineup of Amazon Alexa Tablets will supersede the Fire Tablets entirely. The company will wind down production of its old product and sell the remaining stock over the next few months. Once those Fire tablets sell out, Amazon has committed to providing at least four years of software support, including security and operating system updates.

The Amazon Alexa Tablet lineup

The cloud syncing, Kindle mode and Alexa Plus on-screen intelligence features are packaged into every Alexa Tablet, but these devices aren’t all built the same. The three models have different hardware and peripheral capabilities. Here’s what you can expect from the first wave of Alexa Tablets.

The flagship tablet includes deep AI integration and multiwindowing functionality. It blends work and entertainment capabilities into one device.Tyler Graham/CNET

Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro

Amazon’s new flagship tablet feels like a true jack of all trades. It’s an entertainment hub, an ereader and a personal AI assistant that can be converted into a work laptop using a few simple peripherals.

The most premium configuration has a whopping 16GB of memory, which will help with a more demanding workload for folks who routinely use the device’s multiwindowing capabilities or more complex Play Store applications.

This feels like the platonic ideal of a hybrid device. It’s more portable than a laptop, but has all your favorite mobile apps. It’s powerful enough for some light gaming but you can use it to read a new book, too. It’s not specialized for any particular task, but it can do a bit of everything.  Its launch price is also cheaper than most budget laptops to boot.

16 hours of battery life (20 hours in Kindle mode)

2.8K (2,880×1,920-pixel resolution) LCD screen, 120Hz refresh rate and a 3:2 aspect ratio

Premium configuration with Nanomatte display, new Corning screen with anti-glare properties

Quad Dolby Atmos speakers

MediaTek 8400 Dimensity 8-core CPU

Base configuration: 8GB of RAM, 128GB storage space

Pogo pin connection with new keyboard ($150) and USI 2.0 pen accessory ($90) turn the tablet into a small work laptop or creative device

Starts at $500

The Alexa Tablet 11 may not be quite as large as the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, but it dwarfs the Alexa Tablet 8.Tyler Graham/CNET

Amazon Alexa Tablet 11

This middle-of-the-road Alexa Tablet is likely for people who want the entertainment hub functionality of the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro but are willing to make some compromises to save some money.

The 11-inch model is still able to use a keyboard, but it doesn’t have a physical pogo pin connection. You can still use the stylus to draw on-screen, but there’s less space to do so. More importantly, you’re losing out on the higher storage options available on the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro.

This might not be a portable workstation, but it’s a solid entertainment hub nonetheless: You still get high resolution and all of Amazon’s media is in one place. If you’re looking for a better bargain on a “fun” tablet, the Alexa Tablet 11 could end up being the perfect middle-ground for you.

15 hours of battery life (20 hours in Kindle mode)

Bluetooth keyboard and USI 2.0 pen connection capability

Gray, purple and green color options

Starts at $330

I’m partial to the bright flowery colors that are available for the tiniest Alexa Tablet.Tyler Graham/CNET

Amazon Alexa Tablet 8

The diminutive Alexa Tablet 8 has the same built-in device cloud syncing and Alexa Plus capabilities as the rest of the lineup, but I wouldn’t expect this model to serve as an entertainment hub or work device.

Even though it has full Play Store access, it has less memory and storage space than the more expensive Alexa Tablets. I reckon most people will use this 8.7-inch tablet as a pocket-size ereader in the new and improved Kindle mode, with its additional capabilities serving as a bonus.

I have reservations about introducing in-depth generative AI tools to young children, but I’ve been told these features are gated behind verifiable parental consent and robust content filtering guardrails.Tyler Graham/CNET

The Amazon Kids tablets have been redesigned, too

Just like the regular Fire Tablets, the Fire Kids lineup is going the way of the dodo. But it’s being replaced with two Alexa Tablets that are also built specifically for children. Keith told me the design philosophy for these tablets was to bring them more in line with devices for adults while maintaining safety features and parental controls.

“We know kids want a tablet, not a toy, so we add the same hardware as the Alexa Tablet,” he said. “We ship it with a bumper, a completely different UI and software built just for kids.”

Younger children will benefit from the new 8.7-inch tablet, which has a soft, foam cover around the chassis, while a sleeker 11-inch model will come with a more form-fitting, kid-proof case.

The devices come with the generative-AI Storybuilder tool, which lets kids verbalize stories and see custom visuals for them. This is paired off with its own set of parental controls and a parental dashboard that provides weekly insights on tablet usage. Every Amazon Kids tablet comes with a one-year subscription to Amazon Kids Plus.

The full lineup of Amazon Alexa Tablets is available for preorder now, and will begin shipping out across the US on Oct. 14.

Google has released an experimental note-taking app that can transcribe meetings and audio files entirely offline, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. The app, called Google AI Edge Foresight, is free to use and runs on macOS using the company’s on-device EmbeddingGemma 2 model.

Similar to AI note-taking apps like Granola and Wispr Flow, Foresight summarizes your meetings while providing a space where you can take your own notes. Google says you can jot down shorthand bullet points during your meeting, and the app will transform them into “polished notes” based on the information in the transcript.

Along with transcribing your meetings, Foresight has a built-in assistant you can use to ask questions about what you’ve heard. You can also connect local files to the app, which it can reference when answering your questions. Google says your files, meeting audio, and notes “never leave your computer.”

Google AI Edge Foresight is currently only optimized for Macs with Apple Silicon, but stands out amongst a growing number of AI note-taking apps by operating on-device.

title: Google’s Next Android XR Device Is Arriving Ahead of Meta’s VR Glasses, at a Similar Price
snippet: The Xreal Aura will cost $1,279, and it has some similarities to the Meta VR Glasses coming next year.
fullText:
The once familiar landscape of VR headsets is starting to melt. As smart glasses flood the zone, VR devices are changing form. And devices that are almost VR, too. Meta’s glasses-like headset, called Meta VR Glasses, is coming next year for $1,299, but the Xreal Aura, a pair of display glasses with a computer puck that also turns into an AR/VR device, is coming even sooner for $1,279.

Xreal announced the Aura’s price on Wednesday, but not a release date. It should be coming in the next month or two, though, and I’ve had a chance to try it several times over the last year. It’s currently only available to preorder if you placed a $100 hold for the right to order one earlier this year, but more options to buy are coming in a few weeks, according to the company.

Xreal’s Project Aura supports hand tracking, and it works just like it does on VR headsets to pinch, scroll and control apps.

Scott Stein/CNET

What Xreal Aura can do

I found the Xreal Aura to be one of the most fascinating devices I’ve tried in a while, because it bridges some of the gaps between glasses, AR and VR. The Aura is a more advanced pair of Xreal display glasses (which I’ve reviewed in various forms over the last few years) connected to a processing puck that runs Android XR, floating apps and experiences into the world with micro-OLED displays. The displays are effectively mirrored down from the top of the glasses and projected over transparent lenses that have layers of dimming. Google’s visually aware Gemini AI can run at the same time, recognizing apps that are open and things in the real world around you.

			

More from CNET

The Aura has a larger 70-degree field of view than previous Xreal glasses (which top out at 57 degrees), which allows more viewing space and more apps to be laid out. It’s less than standard VR, but in my demos, it felt like it approached usefulness close to what VR headsets can offer. It also has hand tracking via external cameras, and can float 3D experiences and even VR apps in Android XR into the room surprisingly well.

The $1,279 starting price for Xreal Aura includes 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM. There’s also a $1,500 version with 512GB of storage and 16GB of RAM.

The Aura comes with its own travel case. The processor puck it uses is about the size of a phone.

Scott Stein/CNET

Meta VR Glasses and Xreal Aura compared

Meta’s VR Glasses have a similar, yet different, proposition. They’re more like sliced-off Apple Vision Pros and use pass-through cameras to let you see the outside world rather than actually transparent lenses. But they also have eye tracking in addition to hand tracking, and can work with Meta Quest controllers and Quest apps. Their 84-degree field-of-view micro-OLED displays are more expansive and higher-res than the Aura’s. Meta’s VR Glasses have only one storage config we know of (128GB), but also have a MicroSD card slot that can store apps too.

Both the Xreal Aura and the Meta VR Glasses connect with external processing pucks that are roughly phone-sized, both using Qualcomm Snapdragon XR Elite chipsets. Both also have the unique ability to port in other USB-C video-out devices, floating a phone screen, laptop, iPad or Steam Deck right alongside other apps. Clearly, a phase change in form is underway.

Google’s got more glasses coming

Google’s got lots of Android XR devices planned, including a line of Gemini-powered smart glasses made with Samsung, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster coming sometime before the end of the year. But the Xreal Aura is Google’s next Android XR product on deck since its Samsung Galaxy XR partnership last year, and can do a lot of the same things in a smaller form for less. 

Between the Meta VR Glasses and the Xreal Aura, it already feels like the distinctions between “VR” and “AR” are starting to melt away. But at their almost-identical near-$1,300 prices, they’re also setting the tone for what these gadgets will cost going forward. Valve’s Steam Frame VR headset is over $1,000, and Snap’s upcoming Specs AR glasses cost $2,195. At these prices, although far less than Apple’s $3,699 Vision Pro, they’re also far more expensive than Meta’s Quest VR headsets. If you’re considering spending up on the idea of immersive displays that can be used for work or taken on the go, though, you should stay put and see how these devices perform when I review them.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Scott Stein

Other obsessions include magic, immersive theater, puzzles, board games, cooking, improv and the New York Jets. My background includes an MFA in theater which I apply to thinking about immersive experiences of the future.

title: Asos confirms breach of customer data after hackers send rogue app notification
snippet: The hackers alerted the fashion giant's customers through a push notification that said they had "fully compromised" the company's cloud storage.
fullText:
UK fashion retail giant Asos has confirmed a data breach of its customers’ personal information after hackers used the company’s own app to notify users that the company had been compromised.

Asos said in a filing with the London Stock Exchange that hackers broke into a third-party platform hosting data that the company uses to communicate with customers. 

The company said that names and contact information were taken in the breach. 

BBC News reports that the stolen data includes home addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, as well as notes relating to customer profiles, such as their website search queries.

Asos said the hackers sent an “unauthorised customer notification,” which many posted to social media. The notification addressed Asos’ data protection officer and IT department and said that the hackers “fully compromised” the company’s data hosted on Snowflake, a tech company that allows its corporate customers to analyze large amounts of data. “Engage with us, or we will leak it,” the notification reads.

By using the app’s own notification system to alert customers, the hackers are trying to pressure the company into engaging with them or risk having the stolen data published online.

The hackers reportedly broke into the Snowflake instance by “impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials,” reports Bleeping Computer. Snowflake said it had not experienced a breach of its systems. It’s unclear if the Asos-run Snowflake instance was protected with multi-factor authentication. It’s also not known how the hackers gained access to Asos’ system for sending in-app push notifications, which is often handled by a third-party service. 

The hackers, who go by the handle Xuanye Group, have not indicated how much data they allegedly possess. Asos has 17 million customers, according to its website.

Earlier this year, fintech giant Betterment was compromised by hackers who used their access to the company’s third-party marketing platform to impersonate the company and send a crypto scam to its customers. The hackers also access customer names, email addresses, and phone numbers, among other data, during the breach.

title: Apple overtakes Samsung to lead European carrier smartphone sales in Q2, per report
snippet: A new report from Counterpoint Research shows that Apple overtook Samsung during the second quarter of 2026 to become the leading smartphone brand in Europe’s carrier channel, as operator sales held up better than the broader market. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new report from Counterpoint Research shows that Apple overtook Samsung during the second quarter of 2026 to become the leading smartphone brand in Europe’s carrier channel, as operator sales held up better than the broader market. Here are the details.

Apple helps carrier sales outperform broader European smartphone market

In a report published today, Counterpoint Research says smartphone sales through carriers in Europe declined 4% year-over-year in Q2 2026, compared with an 11% drop in the open market. Total smartphone sales, per the report, declined 8%.

Apple was a key driver of this shift, having overtaken Samsung as the market share leader of Europe’s operator channel. Motorola and vivo also contributed to the growth with some strategic positioning with key European operators.

Counterpoint says this is yet another result of rising memory costs, which have hit Europe’s low-end smartphone market particularly hard. Carrier sales, meanwhile, have held up better because they tend to skew toward higher-end devices and premium brands such as Apple, with more phones purchased on contract.

According to the report, Apple’s share of smartphone sales through European carriers rose from 33% in Q2 2025 to 37% in Q2 2026, while Samsung’s fell from 39% to 34% over the same period.

That said, Chinese brand vivo posted the biggest year-over-year increase in carrier sales, at 90%, while Motorola came in a distant second with 27% growth.

Here’s Jan Stryjak, Associate Director at Counterpoint Research, on these numbers:

“Smartphone sales through operators in Europe are typically more high-end than through the open market, as more are purchased on a contract. They are also more skewed towards more premium brands like Apple, Samsung, and Google. The collapse of the low-end of the smartphone market so far in 2026 because of the memory price crisis has therefore benefitted the operator channel, which has declined comparatively less than the open market.”

Stryjak added that he expects the carrier channel to continue gaining share over the “next few quarters as the lower end of the market continues to be impacted by the memory crisis.” He also noted that independent retailers have increased promotional activity compared to carriers, “which could mitigate some of the price rises and provide addition [sic] stimulus to the open market.”

title: GPT-6 for All: Your ChatGPT Answers Are Getting a Very Visual Makeover
snippet: New interactive graphics are powered by GPT-6, which is rolling out to free users now.
fullText:
OpenAI has been working this year to make ChatGPT more than a text-only service. Now, it’s rolling out a new intelligent user interface to bring interactive graphics, images and other visual displays into your AI answers, powered by GPT-6. The interface will be available to free users this week.

If you ask ChatGPT to explain the offside rule in soccer, the chatbot could create interactive graphics that let you adjust each player’s position on the field to see where the boundary lines would be in each scenario. You can also have the AI plan your dinner party menu and grocery list, with a slider you can adjust based on the expected number of guests. ChatGPT creates these custom images and graphics, but they’re based on information pulled from online sources, which should be cited in each answer.

Your next answer from ChatGPT might have more images and interactive elements.OpenAI

This new UI is powered by OpenAI’s latest flagship model, GPT-6. In addition to the new answer format, all ChatGPT users will have access to GPT-6 this week. It’s rolling out to Plus and Pro users on Wednesday, with plans to bring it to free users later in the week.

			

More from CNET

More complex tasks for AI models — like deep reasoning, image generation and running AI agents — eat up users’ allotted tokens or usage limits. OpenAI told CNET that while there’s more information in these AI images, it doesn’t expect this new visual interface to “meaningfully” change usage because “by and large it’s very efficient.” We’ll have to wait and see if that proves true for most users.

Despite being the company that made tech history with its text-synthesis AI model, OpenAI has worked to move its chatbot beyond text alone. It has invested in its voice mode, with new AI voice models that are better at conversation and language translation. Its image generation efforts, including ChatGPT Images 2.5, are also bolstering the company’s efforts to create more multimodal experiences for customers. The idea is to give users more options to customize how they use ChatGPT. But for now, this new intelligent user interface is limited to text prompts, though you can use voice-to-text to dictate your requests, OpenAI says.

title: The best CarPlay upgrades to try in iOS 27
snippet: Apple released iOS 27 to everyone a few weeks ago, and it includes several CarPlay changes worth checking out. Here are a few changes I’ve been loving so far. more…
fullText:
Apple released iOS 27 to everyone a few weeks ago, and it includes several CarPlay changes worth checking out. Here are a few changes I’ve been loving so far.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Sony is running a massive sale on its best BRAVIA TVs, ranging from its entry-level to flagship options — shop now to save! 

CarPlay features to try in iOS 27

Siri AI

Siri AI is the flagship feature of iOS 27, and it extends to CarPlay. In fact, I’ve found it to be especially useful via CarPlay. Siri AI can answer questions around your personal context, world knowledge, and much more in iOS 27.

For example, you can ask Siri to find a specific address or location in your email or text messages, then begin routing to that location, all while using just your voice.

Robust, hands-free control is important in the car, and iOS 27 finally gives Siri the power that it deserves in CarPlay.

Now Playing changes

CarPlay in iOS 27 offers a persistent “Now Playing” MiniPlayer throughout audio apps. This appears in the upper-right corner of the interface and shows playback controls and album artwork.

The Now Playing interface in CarPlay has also been updated to include an audio scrubber at long last. You can drag the scrubber to easily skip to different parts of a song or podcast without using steering wheel controls or reaching for your iPhone.

New wallpapers

CarPlay isn’t known for its robust collection of wallpapers, and Apple doesn’t let you use your own photos for some reason.

In iOS 27, Apple has at least added a collection of new wallpapers that you can choose from. They are similar to the stock iOS 27 wallpapers available on iPhone.

Stability improvements

iOS 27 focuses a lot on platform improvements to performance and reliability, and that applies to CarPlay too. Apple says iOS 27 addresses two key things in CarPlay:

Improved navigation heading and GPS accuracy in CarPlay

Improved wireless CarPlay reliability

So if you’ve ever had problems with those two things in CarPlay, it’s possible that iOS 27 makes the experience much better.

Coming soon(ish): Video app support

Finally, Apple says that developers can now make dedicated video apps for CarPlay in iOS 27. The feature, however, requires support from automakers. This means it might be a while before you can actually use any video apps with CarPlay in your vehicle.

Wrap up

While the dream for many people is still CarPlay Ultra, it’s really nice to see Apple make meaningful improvements to the version of CarPlay already available in millions of cars on the road today.

Have you updated to iOS 27? What CarPlay changes have you noticed? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Apple TV’s latest acquisition signals key shift for streamer
snippet: Apple TV just acquired the global streaming rights to Dustfall, a crime series from Australia and the second recent deviation from the streamer’s originals-only strategy. more…
fullText:
Apple TV just acquired the global streaming rights to Dustfall, a crime series from Australia and the second recent deviation from the streamer’s originals-only strategy.

Apple has started licensing more TV series, deviating from all-originals strategy

Ever since Apple TV launched in 2019, it rejected the typical streaming approach of licensing existing content and instead prioritized originals.

Apple has been remarkably consistent with its originals-only strategy. Until recently, the only exceptions have been children’s content that complement its originals (like Peanuts holiday specials), and limited-time bonus films.

But that changed this week, when acclaimed comedy Small Prophets premiered after Apple acquired the rights to the British breakout hit over the summer.

Small Prophets seems like a savvy acquisition. Early reviews call it a “masterpiece” and perhaps “the finest show to hit Apple this year.”

Now today, Apple has announced a second acquisition. Dustfall, an Anna Torv-starring crime series that originated in Australia, will join the streamer in 2027.

Like Small Prophets, Dustfall was created by an international production company and will air in select territories overseas before its global Apple TV premiere.

Clearly, Apple sees acquisitions differently than it once did.

While the streamer isn’t abandoning its successful original-first approach, licensing high-quality series from around the world to beef up its catalog is very much a strategic shift.

And it’s one I’m curious if we’ll see accelerate moving forward.

What do you think of Apple TV licensing third-party series? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month, or you can get it discounted through the Apple One bundle.

fullText:
Emma Roth

 

is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Google is launching a “universal” Gemini AI agent that can work across apps and devices in the background. The tool, announced as part of the Gemini at Work event on Thursday, will be available within the Gemini Enterprise app, allowing users to chat with the Gemini agent and assign it tasks from a single interface.

In addition to having Gemini work directly inside Workspace apps like Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, and others, users can interact with the agent from their mobile device, desktop computer, the web, and third-party apps like Slack or Microsoft 365. Since it runs in the cloud, Gemini will maintain the same context across all connected devices.

Google says Gemini can also work with job-specific sub-agents to complete tasks, as well as operate as a “coworker agent” with a dedicated identity and its own “@agents.company.com” email. Gemini will automatically perform tasks using an AI model that best fits the job.

The Gemini agent is currently only available to enterprise customers in private preview, but it may offer a glimpse into Google’s broader vision for the AI assistant that can answer questions and perform work for you from a single window. Google previously launched its consumer-facing Gemini Spark agent in May, which subscribers can use to perform tasks across Workspace and on the web, but it’s available through a separate interface within the Gemini app.

title: Waymo locks in $5B loan from Blackstone, PIMCO to fuel robotaxi expansion
snippet: This is the first time the Alphabet-owned company has turned to debt financing.
fullText:
Waymo, the autonomous vehicle technology company under Google parent Alphabet, closed a $5 billion loan from a series of high-profile lenders, including PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street. 

The debt financing — Waymo’s first — comes as the company accelerates its commercial expansion within existing cities while pushing into new markets in the United States, Europe, and Japan. Waymo described the debt financing as an important step in its evolution into a “scaling commercial enterprise.”

Other lenders in the $5 billion loan include Capital Group, Loomis Sayles, T. Rowe Price, Apollo, Blue Owl, Diameter Capital Partners, Franklin Templeton, Fidelity Management & Research Company, HPS Investment Partners, and Oaktree, Waymo said on Thursday. Goldman Sachs served as the sole lead bookrunner.

Until now, Waymo has relied on capital from its parent company and outside investors. In February, Waymo raised $16 billion in equity from investors that pushed its valuation to $126 billion. Dragoneer Investment Group, DST Global, and Sequoia Capital led the funding round. Alphabet, which supported the round, has maintained its position as majority investor. The company raised $5.6 billion in a Series C funding round in 2024, $2.5 billion in 2021, and $3.2 billion in 2020. 

A Waymo spokesperson said in an email that the debt financing will give the company financial flexibility to strengthen its balance sheet and position it to “capitalize on the significant opportunities ahead, especially as a scaling business with proven commercial demand and improved road safety outcomes in the communities in which we operate.” 

Formerly a self-driving project within Google, Waymo spent years testing its autonomous vehicle tech on public roads in Silicon Valley and the Bay Area and providing the occasional public or media demo. The company expanded in 2016 to Phoenix, which would become its first robotaxi market.

In August 2023, Waymo received the final necessary permit to operate a robotaxi service and charge for rides in California, a milestone that would kick off a more aggressive commercial playbook. Since then, Waymo has launched in multiple California cities, including Los Angeles, San Francisco, and, more recently San Diego. It has also brought its robotaxi service to numerous other U.S. markets, including Austin, Dallas, and Houston in Texas and Miami, Orlando, and Tampa in Florida. Waymo now offers robotaxi services in 15 markets.

Waymo is keen to take its robotaxi services global, too. The company is testing in London and Tokyo and plans to launch in those cities.

The company’s growth has also spurred criticism and increased attention from regulators. 

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation opened an investigation into the illegal behavior of Waymo robotaxis around school buses. The federal safety regulator also launched an investigation after a Waymo robotaxi hit a child near a school. The child, who sustained minor injuries, was struck at about six mph. Earlier this year, the National Transportation Safety Board opened its own investigation into Waymo after its robotaxis were spotted illegally passing stopped school buses numerous times in at least two states.

She is currently the transportation editor at TechCrunch and co-host of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast. She is also co-founder and co-host of the podcast, “The Autonocast.” She previously wrote for Fortune, The Verge, Bloomberg, MIT Technology Review and CBS Interactive.

title: New MacBook Pro leak could be very good news for ‘pro’ users
snippet: Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro is coming soon, and the latest leak offers potentially great news for truly ‘pro’ users worried about the rumored thinner design. more…
fullText:
Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro is coming soon, and the latest leak offers potentially great news for truly ‘pro’ users worried about the rumored thinner design.

Redesigned MacBook Pro will be much lighter, but not ‘significantly thinner,’ per Mark Gurman

The MacBook Pro has long attracted customers who may not be ‘pros’ in the sense of doing professional coding work, video editing, photography, or other tasks that require extra computing power.

Plenty of people want a MacBook Pro simply because it’s the best laptop Apple sells. It has the best display in a Mac, the most power, and the longest battery life.

But a new MacBook Pro design is coming, and previous reporting has said it will be thinner and lighter than the current model. Earlier this week Mark Gurman even said it will be “significantly” lighter.

That might sound great to ‘prosumers’ like myself, but it probably raises alarm bells for true ‘pros.’

Last night in a post on X though, Mark Gurman offered good news:

I don’t think it’ll be significantly thinner in the end

— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) October 7, 2026

Thinner, but not significantly so, while still offering a big weight reduction, sounds like exactly the right balance that should please most users.

If the new design doesn’t bring a drastic reduction in thickness, that’s good news for at least three reasons. It means the new MacBook Pro should:

Retain all or most of its existing ports

Offer battery life that’s not far off from current models

Have plenty of thermal headroom

Weight is generally a more common complaint than thickness with the current MacBook Pro, so if Apple can make the new MacBook Pro easier to carry, slim it down a bit, and still offer the kind of power and versatility pros need, that sounds like a big win.

What’s your take on the new MacBook Pro design based on rumors? Let us know in the comments.

title: Spotify starts rolling out audiobooks to more than 180 markets
snippet: Spotify today announced a global rollout of its audiobooks section, giving users in more than 180 markets access to over 350,000 titles spanning more than 120 languages. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Spotify today announced a global rollout of its audiobooks section, giving users in more than 180 markets access to over 350,000 titles spanning more than 120 languages. Here are the details.

Audiobooks coming to 750+ million Spotify users

Four years after launching audiobooks in the U.S., and following a rather limited expansion into select countries in the years since, Spotify today announced that audiobooks are finally coming to more than 180 markets.

As Spotify explained in a blog post, the rollout begins today and will continue through the end of 2026, expanding audiobook access from 22 markets to more than 180 and making the service available to more than 750 million people worldwide.

Users in newly supported markets will have access to more than 350,000 titles, with additional catalogs available in Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Polish, and other languages.

Access will vary depending on the market. Eligible Premium subscribers in countries including Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Poland, Chile, Norway, Peru, Italy, Spain, and Portugal will get 12 hours of audiobook listening each month as part of their existing subscription.

Spotify is also expanding Audiobooks+, an add-on that gives subscribers additional listening hours each month. The service will serve as the primary way to access audiobooks in markets across Africa and Asia, as well as Argentina.

Users will also be able to purchase individual audiobooks outright, while pricing and availability will vary by market.

The company also announced an update to Page Match, its feature for switching between physical or digital books and their audiobook versions. Users can now scan a book’s ISBN barcode, and then enter a page number to find the corresponding point in the audiobook. Spotify added that the feature now works in more than 30 languages.

Audiobooks+ is also expanding to Student plans in Ireland, Belgium, Austria, and Finland beginning in November. Spotify says the add-on has surpassed 1 million subscribers since launching just over a year ago and now generates more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue.

According to Spotify, monthly audiobook listeners grew nearly 40% over the past year, while total listening hours increased by more than 30%.

title: Googlebook Glowbar doesn’t have the ‘knock-knock’ Chromebook Pixel battery gesture
snippet: One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before. more…
fullText:
One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before.

The original Chromebook Pixel launched in 2013 as the launchpad for ChromeOS. To this day, it remains a pretty incredible piece of hardware design, though it was inherently flawed with a truly atrocious display and a sky-high price tag to boot, not to mention an even more restricted operating system compared to what ChromeOS would eventually morph into. Still, it earned a follow-up in 2015’s Chromebook Pixel which delivered a lot of key upgrades.

Both models included a signature hardware feature in the four-piece “light bar” across the top of the lid. It was mainly a design element to ring in the Chrome connection with the four colors of the Chrome and Google logos. It lived on in the later, yet short-lived Pixel C tablet. 

It also served a somewhat practical purpose, too.

	

When you would plug in a Chromebook Pixel, the light bar would give you a rough idea of how much charge was already in the battery. Beyond that, a fun little “knock-knock” gesture on the lid would tell you the same information, but whenever the laptop was just out. You could tap the lid and get an idea of the battery status without opening it up or plugging it in, which was especially useful in a time where laptop battery was still very much Not Great.

It’s that gesture that’s gone on Googlebook’s Glowbar, which retains the light-up action when you plug it in, but loses the “knock-knock” that really grabbed everyone’s attention when Google first launched it. 

What can the Glowbar do? 

Like Chromebook Pixel, it does light up when you plug the machine into power, showing battery status both when it plugged in and unplugged. Useful! It’s also more granular than it was on that older hardware. The only other function, besides an animation when you close the lid, is interaction with Gemini. I struggle to see the utility in that one given the Glowbar is at the back of the display, but I guess why not?

title: Google Labs announces ‘Playground’ for prompt-based game creation
snippet: Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.”

This Google Labs experiment leverages  Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria models with a “custom harness to make game creation more accessible.”

It starts with a chat interface that lets you “direct the game just by typing what you want to build.” You can decide between a 2D or 3D game and specify whether it’s single or multi-player. Google offers starter prompts that you can remix and a guided development experience.

Playground lets you “tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment.”

	

Google today also previewed a Unity Spark integration that allows for “robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities, and the flexibility of the Unity runtime.”

The accessibility of Playground and world-class game-building expertise of Unity provides the building blocks for an ecosystem where users can start with a simple text prompt and eventually grow into building immersive experiences with Unity

These are browser-based games that are playable on phone or laptop. Once you’re done, games can be kept private, shared via link, or published to the Playground Explore gallery for everyone. Titles go through safety (community guideline) screening along with user reporting.

Players can rate games, while there’s support for in-game leaderboards with Play Games profile integration.

Google is rolling out Playground starting in the US. Free users will be able to generate games, with expanded access tied to Google One membership.

title: Apple killed the Mac mini’s best hidden feature [Video]
snippet: With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value. more…
fullText:
With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value.

When it first launched, the M4 Mac mini provided a huge bang for the buck. Not only did it feature Apple’s M4 SoC, but it also came with a healthy 16GB of unified memory, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, two front-facing USB 3 ports, HDMI, and Ethernet. At just $599 or $499 at the student discount price, the M4 Mac mini was not only the most versatile Mac in Apple’s lineup but also, pound for pound, the best Mac in the lineup. 

Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

But Apple’s smallest Mac had a secret up its sleeve that made it an even more valuable machine: a slot for upgradable storage. Users could literally pry open the machine’s back cover, unscrew a few screws, and access a removable NAND module that could be easily replaced with a third-party SSD up to 2TB.

The benefits were multifaceted. Not only could you upgrade the SSD or easily fix a drive that failed, but you could also save some serious coin by forgoing Apple’s build-to-order upgrade option and do it yourself with a much cheaper third-party SSD. 

Upgrading the M4 Mac mini SSD

At the time, Apple charged $800 for the 2TB upgrade, transforming the “budget” computer into a $1400 computer with the click of an option. By upgrading after purchase with a third-party SSD, users could save nearly $500.

Of course, as someone who likes to tinker, I was extremely excited about this and ended up posting a full video tutorial showing, step by step, how to upgrade the stock SSD with a third-party drive. It proved to be quite popular, amassing half a million views. 

Video: How to upgrade the M4 Mac mini SSD

It was nice while it lasted.

With the launch of this latest generation of Mac mini, Apple has soldered the SSD directly to the logic board, effectively eliminating the ability to upgrade it post-purchase with a third-party NAND module.

The Mac mini has gone from what was hands-down the best bang-for-your-buck Mac to a significantly more expensive product, not just for the base model, which goes from $600 to $900, but also for the 2TB upgrade, which goes from $800 to $1000. 

Today if you want an M6 Mac mini with a 2TB SSD, you’ll need to pay Apple $1900. The equivalent M4 Mac mini, with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade, would have set you back roughly $920 when you factor in the $320 aftermarket upgrade price being charged at the time. Obviously, things have gotten more expensive, so it’s not exactly Apple’s to Apple’s (see what I did there), but that’s a $1000 increase in price, not only because Apple is charging significantly more, but also because Apple eliminated the ability for customers to upgrade the machines themselves.

I have a good idea as to why Apple opted to increase the price of the base Mac mini by $300, and I can even understand why its SSD prices have increased so much. Because of AI and other factors, component, SSD, and memory prices have all skyrocketed. But that doesn’t explain why Apple opted to solder the SSDs to the logic board instead of keeping them user-replaceable like before.

	

We can speculate, but we may never know the real answer for Apple’s decision to revert back to soldered SSDs. What we do know, however, is that these machines are significantly more expensive, and even that sounds like an understatement. In the case of the M4 Mac mini with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade vs the M6 Mac mini with a 2TB build-to-order upgrade, it’s roughly a 106% price increase.

9to5Mac’s Take

It can be difficult to find a base model M4 Mac mini on the used market at a reasonable price, but if you can manage to do so, it remains an excellent machine for its baseline performance, features, and upgradable SSD.

The good news in all of this is that all of Apple’s Mac mini models come with Thunderbolt connectivity, so you can easily add high-bandwidth external storage via a USB or Thunderbolt SSD. I’m personally a big fan of the Samsung T9, which offers a relatively affordable way to add extra storage. 

What do you think Apple’s reasoning is for getting rid of user-replaceable SSDs in the Mac mini? Do you have any particular theories? Sound off in the comments with your thoughts.

fullText:

title: Googlebook’s Android-integrated features won’t work with Samsung phones at launch
snippet: Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features. more…
fullText:
Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features.

Built on top of Android, Googlebook’s core pitch is to be the laptop for Android users, with deep integration between your smartphone and laptop. This includes a host of features such as instant hotspot, notification sync, phone file access, and the ability to continue tasks started on your phone from your Googlebook laptop. You can also stream apps from your phone’s display to your Googlebook directly.

In terms of deep integration, is a good pitch, but it won’t work for a lot of users at launch.

On a support page, Google confirms that Googlebook’s suite of Android integrations won’t work with any device running Android 16 or prior – Android 17 is the minimum requirement. 

	

Beyond that, Google also confirmed that Samsung devices are not supported at launch. Rather, support is rolling out “over the coming weeks.” It’s not mentioned whether Google or Samsung needs to push an update here, but it stands to reason that an update on Samsung’s end might be needed.

Support for Better Together features will be rolling out across all Android 17-supported Samsung devices over the coming weeks. Sorry for the inconvenience!

Meanwhile, Googlebook faces some other early hiccups, such as lacking support for Slack’s web app at launch, a key workplace app, as well as some apparent optimization issues for apps running on Intel hardware.

title: Claude launches Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides integration with sidebar and more
snippet: If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. more…
fullText:
If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.

You can already use Gemini natively in Google Workspace apps, but those invested in Claude can now use their AI of choice inside of Google’s ecosystem through the Claude for Google Workspace add-on which is in public beta starting today.
